clue.text: Game for some music?

definitions.meaning: a bar-billiards style table game in which balls are knocked into numbered holes
a short, light piece of music, usually for piano

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which game to play to go along with a bit of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small-table pub game with cues and pins and a trifling, light composition such as Beethoven's piano pieces.

clue.text: "Face-flatterer and ______ are the same." (Tennyson)

parts.note: a quotation with a gap: fill in the word Tennyson paired with a face-flatterer, one who speaks ill of others behind their backs

explanation.surface: A line from Tennyson saying the flatterer and the one who slanders behind your back are alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank in the quotation; the missing word, from Tennyson's Merlin and Vivien, means someone who slanders people behind their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who slanders others when they are absent, the opposite face of a flatterer.

clue.text: Class seeing rising sun for example

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A class watching the sunrise as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a classification grouping in biology, a class of related species.

clue.text: Nurses taking trouble in preparing what's left

indicators.note: taking says the word for nurses holds the word for trouble inside it

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or look after
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Nurses take pains getting leftovers ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in preparing' is linking padding here, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps and remnants at the end of something are what remain.

clue.text: Cut the allowance for a knight

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as with a boil
a lot is a share or portion allotted to someone

explanation.surface: Someone trims a knight's allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the foremost knight of King Arthur's court.

clue.text: In ten letters, get very cold but lead on

indicators.note: the letters of the word ten are taken and put into a different order

parts.note: to ice is to freeze or become icy

explanation.surface: Someone writes ten letters, gets chilled, yet carries on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ten letters' means rearrange the letters of TEN to give ENT; 'lead on' is the definition, not 'carry on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone along.

clue.text: The poet is inflamed with passion

definitions.meaning: to blaze with strong feeling, as with love or anger

explanation.surface: A poet is described as on fire with ardent feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns is the Scottish bard, and a person who glows with fierce desire is said to be on fire that way.

clue.text: Essayist's absorbing English guide

indicators.note: absorbing says the essayist's name takes the English letter into itself

parts.note: Francis Bacon wrote famous Essays

explanation.surface: An essayist's absorbing guide to English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing English guide' reads as a gripping book; Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan essayist, absorbs E.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal fire or light that guides ships or travellers is a beacon.

clue.text: Put a salesman on edge and the outcome will be a telling-off

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the salesman is placed above the edge

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rim is an edge
taken as written

explanation.surface: Making a salesman nervous will get him reprimanded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous; here a REP is placed on a RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal rebuke or scolding is a telling-off.

clue.text: Youth has a way with the goody-goody!

parts.note: S, south, is a compass direction and so a way to go
a prig is a self-righteous, goody-goody person

explanation.surface: A young man knows how to handle a self-righteous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a way with' reads as having a knack; a sprig is an old word for a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a dated word for a young fellow, a scion or stripling.

clue.text: Hand over evidence after study

indicators.note: after says the word for evidence follows the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a sign is an indication or piece of evidence

explanation.surface: Proof is handed in once it has been examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To consign goods is to deliver or entrust them to another's keeping.

clue.text: He must have a gin or two when at work

definitions.text: He must have a gin or two when at work

parts.words: He must have a gin or two when at work
parts.note: reads like a worker who needs a drink on the job, but the gin is a snare for catching animals

explanation.surface: A man who cannot get through the working day without a couple of gins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the spirit, but a gin is also an animal snare, so this is a man whose work is setting snares.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter of fur-bearing animals sets snares, and a gin is one kind of snare.

clue.text: Scholars the heartless thrash

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates and so scholars

indicators.note: heartless says the middle letter of the word the is removed

explanation.surface: A grim scene of learned men beating someone without mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like it describes the scholars, but it strips the middle letter H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste someone is an old, informal word for beating or thrashing them soundly.

clue.text: Fencing long since vandalised

indicators.note: something vandalised has been smashed about, so these letters are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fence that has stood for years has been smashed up by vandals.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing a field is surrounding it, shutting it in on every side.

clue.text: Depression could well result in its falling

definitions.text: Depression could well result in its falling

parts.words: Depression could well result in its falling
parts.note: reads like an economic slump causing something to drop, but sadness makes a drop of salty water fall from the eye

explanation.surface: An economist warns that a slump may bring something crashing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests economics or weather; here it is low spirits, which can lead to weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop shed from the eye in weeping is what sadness may bring to fall down a cheek.

clue.text: No ale? Ring for it maybe — it's strengthening

indicators.note: maybe says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: No beer? Then ring for some, as a pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: An angle iron is an L-shaped metal strip used to strengthen joints and frames.
explanation.definitionFit: An L-section metal bar used to reinforce a structure gives it strength.

clue.text: A state service

definitions.meaning: .... is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state
a celebration of the Eucharist in church

explanation.surface: Something described as a public, official service.
explanation.definitionFit: Massachusetts is abbreviated that way, and the word is also the Eucharist celebrated as a church rite.

clue.text: Dogs' jumpers

definitions.meaning: spaniels of the breed used to flush game

explanation.surface: Sweaters knitted for dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' reads as British for sweaters, but it means leapers; springer spaniels are a gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Springer spaniels are a gundog breed, and anything that springs is a leaper.

clue.text: Seize the goods when first seen in the Channel

indicators.note: seen in says the word for first appears inside the word for channel

parts.note: a drain is a channel for carrying away water
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Contraband goods are seized as soon as they appear in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Channel' suggests the sea between England and France; here it is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is a legal term for seizing property to pay a debt.

clue.text: It has to do with wanting to be firm and natural

definitions.text: It has to do with wanting

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
native means innate or natural, as in native wit

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to be resolute and unaffected.
explanation.walkthrough: Conative is a psychology term describing the striving or desiring side of the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology, conation is the faculty of desire and will, and conative describes it.

clue.text: The right time of life for passion

parts.note: an age is a period or stage of life

explanation.surface: Someone claims there is a proper age for falling in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Passion in the sense of violent anger or fury.

clue.text: Underworld organisation causing chaos

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for Hades itself
an order is an organised society, such as a religious or chivalric body

explanation.surface: A criminal gang is stirring up mayhem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld organisation' reads as the Mafia, but Dis is the classical underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of confusion and lack of arrangement is chaos.

clue.text: Polish soldiers (first-class)

parts.note: the RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British soldiers
fine means excellent or first-class

explanation.surface: Top-quality soldiers from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' reads as from Poland; it is the verb to polish.
explanation.definitionFit: To refine something is to polish or improve it.

clue.text: The German admitting everyone to American place

indicators.note: admitting says the German article lets everyone inside it

parts.note: das is a German word for the
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A German lets everyone in to an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dallas is a city in Texas.

clue.text: Quite without grace, but gentle in a strange way

indicators.note: strange way says the letters are put into an odd new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is gentle yet oddly clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking elegance means clumsy, without grace or refinement.

clue.text: Meet with some disdain. -.curious

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone meets a mixture of disdain and curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to meet with it or bring it on oneself.

clue.text: A guy will go about one with all speed

indicators.note: go about says one word wraps around another

parts.note: a guy is a man or fellow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man hurries off to deal with a matter as fast as he can.
explanation.walkthrough: Amain is an old word meaning at full speed or with full force.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb for doing something at full force or speed, as in old sea stories.

clue.text: The trouble about love

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Love causes all sorts of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to love deeply.

clue.text: Warm drink prepared from fruit

definitions.meaning: warm in the sense of friendly and hearty
a sweet fruit syrup diluted to drink, such as lime juice concentrate

explanation.surface: A hot beverage made from fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means friendly and hearty; as a noun it is a sweetened fruit syrup drink.

clue.text: Dope is a treatment for fat

indicators.note: a treatment is a working or handling of material, so these letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug is offered as a cure for obesity.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for fatty tissue in the body.

clue.text: Old kitchen equipment set in a row

definitions.meaning: an old-style cooking stove with hotplates and ovens
to arrange things in a line

explanation.surface: Antique kitchenware is lined up neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen stove of the old cast-iron kind has that name, and to line up objects in rows is to array them.

clue.text: Unfeeling Oriental coppers look around trainee ship

parts.note: the sen is a small copper coin of Japan and other Far Eastern countries

indicators.note: around says the word for look encloses the trainee's letter

parts.note: to see is to look
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Eastern police officers inspect a training vessel without any feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental coppers' suggests Eastern policemen, but coppers here are copper coins. L is the learner sign on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insensible, unconscious and devoid of sensation is unfeeling.
